note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md (2026-11-28). Wide pictures only (1920x1088). Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper 60% of the frame, clear of the word box. God and the angels are not pictured; Abraham, Sarah, Lot, Hagar, Abimelech and the others are only ordinary people of today, seen from behind, small, or as hands. Fixed recurring objects: Abraham's tent is a small plain weathered tan canvas tent on a simple wooden pole frame; the oak is one huge old oak with a broad gnarled trunk and a wide dark-green crown; Abimelech's town is a walled town of plain flat-roofed pale stone houses with a heavy timber gate, no church, no dome, no steeple and no tower of any kind; the king's hall is a plain large room of pale stone with a long wooden table.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning; (2) write picture ideas for each; (3) judge them; (4) make the top two for each slot as real pictures and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Abraham moves to Gerar and says of Sarah, 'She is my sister', and Abimelech takes her.
God warns Abimelech in a dream that the woman is married and that Abraham, a prophet, will pray for him.
Abimelech tells his servants, then confronts Abraham, who explains his fear and half-truth.
Abimelech gives Sarah back with flocks and silver; Abraham prays, and God heals Abimelech's household.
